A religious leader born in Thatcher, Arizona, at the end of 19th Century said.

> **“Love people, not things; use things, not people.”** ^[https://azquotes.com/author/17656-Spencer_W_Kimball?utm_source=chatgpt.com, **similar formulation appears to have been used earlier by **Joseph Fletcher**, the theologian associated with “situation ethics”: “We ought to love people and use things; the essence of immorality is to love things and use people. [https://exitinterview.biz/quotations/index.htm?utm_source=chatgpt.comhttps://exitinterview.biz/quotations/index.htm?utm_source=chatgpt.com](https://exitinterview.biz/quotations/index.htm?utm_source=chatgpt.com)]

Updated saying might be,

> With people, see potential and set direction. With things, define tolerances and measure outcomes.

> Treat people according to their potential; treat things according to their performance.
